scope: Independent static review of post29 local restore ownership, cleanup accounting, source-proof and privacy boundaries, plus the new diagnostics-only dump-clone observer. Source clearance is not restore execution proof.

resolved_findings.problem: A successful CREATE followed by failed identity read or normalization could leave the clone outside ownedDbs, while cleanup iterated only the map and could incorrectly report disposable_databases_removed=true.
resolved_findings.resolution: Both controllers now record creation attempts before dispatch. Cleanup observes only exact generated names even if no OID was recorded, requires matching name/owner/marker and canonical uint32 OID with zero clients before any drop, rejects a changed known OID, and requires a fresh actual-absence query before cleanup success. An unresolved identity throws into cleanup_unconfirmed and prevents lock release.
resolved_findings.verification: Read current source and three pure ownership test definitions; did not execute them. Recovery agent separately reported nine combined pure tests passing.

reviewed_boundaries: Original29 is queried read-only against the sealed profile and exact full raw catalogue before clone work, with original state/catalogue and existing application/managed-role OIDs, attributes and application-role memberships compared afterward.

Restore corrections accept only six exact historical source/dump representation pairs and require exact full raw catalogue equality afterward. A new29 CHECK representation remains refused until an actual diagnostic observation is reviewed.

Diagnostics observer imports neither the correction planner nor native media stages. It emits safe structural original/clone catalogues and exact raw differences without normalizing or applying corrections.

Database creation and cleanup are limited to generated run-specific names in the already fingerprinted local Docker/PostgreSQL target. No global role DDL, forced session termination, cloud target, provider operation or canonical business mutation is present in the reviewed observer.

Raw dump bytes and exception diagnostics remain private; the observer publishes metadata-only catalogue values, source hashes and bounded status. The recovery bundle validates owned filesystem roots, manifest paths and byte checksums.
Source hashes are checked again before successful observer cleanup/lock release. Existing historical failures and source-history files are preserved.
limits: No current controller run, cleanup, database state, native stage outcome or provider state was verified by this reviewer.

This review clears only the root-authorized diagnostics-only observer source prerequisite. It does not authorize or attest a media retry, a new restore-correction pair, cloud migration, deployed restore, independent-cluster recovery, RTO/RPO or production acceptance.
Private local PostgreSQL identity helpers and recovery bundle source were read; ignored local credential/configuration contents were not opened by this reviewer.
